input: Consolidate my old 401k into my current plan

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The user may have one old 401k or several — and may also be considering an IRA rollover — which changes the number of steps and institutions involved.
Whether the user is handling this entirely themselves or has a financial advisor involved changes who initiates contact and who owns each step.
Knowing whether the old 401k provider and current plan provider have already been identified (and contacted) tells us where in the process the user actually is.
There are tax implications — traditional vs. Roth accounts — and the rollover method (direct vs. indirect) affects whether taxes or penalties apply, which is a hard constraint on the approach.
The immediate next action depends on whether the user needs to gather account statements, call a plan administrator, or complete a specific rollover form — the format of the next step matters.
The user's definition of done — funds fully transferred and confirmed, or just the paperwork initiated — determines how far the plan needs to extend.
Some users want to understand every detail and make active investment choices in the new plan; others just want the money moved with minimal involvement, which affects how much guidance to include.

gold.taskTitle: Roll Over Old 401k Into Current Plan
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to consolidate one or more old 401k accounts from previous employers into their current employer's retirement plan.

questions.title: How many old 401k accounts are you consolidating?
questions.description: Determines whether this is a single rollover or a multi-account consolidation requiring parallel tracks.

questions.title: Have you already contacted your old or current plan provider?
questions.description: Establishes where in the process the user currently stands so the plan starts at the right step.

questions.title: Is your old 401k traditional, Roth, or do you not know?
questions.description: The account type determines tax treatment during the rollover and which receiving account is eligible.

questions.title: Are you working with a financial advisor on this?
questions.description: Identifies who is responsible for key decisions and whether professional guidance is already in the loop.

questions.title: Do you want a direct rollover or will you handle the check yourself?
questions.description: The rollover method — direct institution-to-institution vs. indirect — has different logistics, deadlines, and tax-withholding implications.

questions.title: What does fully done look like to you — funds confirmed and invested?
questions.description: Clarifies whether the plan ends at initiating the transfer or extends to confirming the funds are received and re-invested in the new plan.

questions.title: How hands-on do you want to be with investment choices in the new plan?
questions.description: Determines whether the plan should include a step for selecting new investment allocations or just focus on moving the money.
